metadata.title: SPARC Azure App Service Component Definition

components.title: Azure App Service (Linux container) running SPARC
components.description: Managed PaaS host for the SPARC container. Terminates TLS (HTTPS-only, TLS 1.2 minimum), FTPS disabled, HTTP/2 enabled, system-assigned managed identity, Regional VNet Integration for private outbound to the data tier, optional staging slot for blue/green swaps. Secrets are Key Vault references resolved via the managed identity. Deployed via Terraform (Azure/AAS/modules/app_service/). <!-- UPDATE: insert the Web App resource ID, default hostname, and managed identity principal ID for your deployment. -->

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control implementations for Azure App Service

implemented-requirements.description: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity: The Web App enforces HTTPS-only (https_only=true) with a minimum TLS version of 1.2, so all client traffic is encrypted in transit. FTPS is disabled. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000439, CIS Azure.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: azurerm_linux_web_app.main with https_only=true, site_config.minimum_tls_version="1.2", ftps_state="Disabled".

implemented-requirements.description: Protection of Information at Rest: Application secrets are not stored in app configuration or Terraform state. Sensitive values (DB password, Redis URL, Blob key) are stored in Key Vault and injected as Key Vault references (@Microsoft.KeyVault) resolved at runtime via the app's managed identity. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000429.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: app_settings use @Microsoft.KeyVault(VaultName=...;SecretName=...); azurerm_key_vault_secret for redis-url/blob-access-key; DB secret created by the database module.

implemented-requirements.description: Identification and Authentication: The Web App uses a system-assigned managed identity for Azure resource access (Key Vault secret retrieval) rather than stored credentials. End-user authentication is performed by the SPARC application (OIDC), so App Service built-in authentication is intentionally not enabled. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000148.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: identity { type = "SystemAssigned" } + azurerm_role_assignment granting the principal Key Vault Secrets User.

implemented-requirements.description: Boundary Protection: Outbound access to the private data tier flows through Regional VNet Integration (vnet_route_all_enabled=true) into a delegated subnet; the database, cache, blob, and vault are private (VNet integration / private endpoints, public network access disabled). The Web App is the public inbound tier by design. Reference: DISA SRG-NET-000364.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: virtual_network_subnet_id (integration subnet), vnet_route_all_enabled=true; data tier via Azure/AAS/modules/private_endpoints + delegated DB subnet.

implemented-requirements.description: Event Logging: HTTP, console, audit, and application logs plus AllMetrics are streamed to Log Analytics via a diagnostic setting; detailed error messages and failed-request tracing are enabled. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000089, CIS Azure.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: azurerm_monitor_diagnostic_setting.app (in the monitoring module) with AppServiceHTTPLogs/ConsoleLogs/AuditLogs/AppLogs; logs { detailed_error_messages=true, failed_request_tracing=true }.

implemented-requirements.description: Information Input Validation / availability: App Service probes a configurable health check path and removes unhealthy instances from rotation. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000266.
